title: Miracles of Jesus Christ (The Roman Officer’s servant)
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child narrates Matthew 8:5-13: in Capernaum a Roman officer asks Jesus to heal his paralysed servant, says "just say the word", Jesus praises his great faith and the servant is healed at that hour; lessons: faith, humility, caring for others, praying for the sick.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the healing of the paralysed man.
floor.question: Whose faith did Jesus see when the man was lowered through the roof?
floor.answer: The faith of the man and his friends

representations: a soldier drawn speaking to Jesus
steps: The officer asks for his servant.
Jesus praises his faith; the servant is healed.
contexts: a boss who cares for a worker
a church praying for the hospital

board.do: Write Matthew 8:8: "just say the word, and my servant will be healed".

board.say: Why did the officer not need Jesus to come?

board.do: Wait for the child to say he believed Jesus' word had power.

misconceptions.repair: Read Matthew 8:6: "my servant". Ask why an officer would care so much for a servant.

listen_for: Jesus went to the house and laid hands on him
misconceptions.repair: Read 8:8 and 8:13: "just say the word"; healed at that hour, far away.

misconceptions.ask: What did Jesus say about the officer's faith?
misconceptions.repair: Read 8:10: Jesus was amazed: no one in Israel had such great faith.

misconceptions.ask: Who was the man who asked Jesus to heal his servant (Matthew 8:5)?
misconceptions.repair: Read 8:5 and 8:10: a Roman soldier, an outsider, had greater faith than many in Israel.

checks.question: How was the servant healed?
checks.answer: Jesus spoke and he was healed at that hour
